channel.title: The Way: new studies
channel.description: Personal Bible study notes: the Old and New Testaments read in context, with word studies in the original languages and every claim traceable to a source.

item.title: Partakers of the Divine Nature
item.description: The virtues of 2 Peter 1:3-11 as the fruit of a nature God has given: everything for life and godliness already granted, real effort that is never a burden, the joy that comes with it, and a rich entrance into Christ's kingdom.

item.title: The Judgment Seat of Christ
item.description: Every believer will appear before the judgment seat of Christ to receive reward or loss for what was built on Him. What the Old and New Testaments say about reward, why it is never wages for salvation, how Ezekiel was given his work and held to account for it, how the white robe differs from the fine linen, and why this is a different judgment from the great white throne.

item.title: They Were Given White Robes
item.description: Every white garment God's people wear in Scripture, from the garments of skins in Eden to the robes washed in the Lamb's blood and the Bride's fine linen: who wears them, what makes them white, and why every one of them is God's gift.

item.title: Saved as Through Fire
item.description: Paul says a believer who builds with the world's wisdom is saved, but only as one escaping through the flames (1 Corinthians 3:15). Jude sends the church to snatch the drifting out of the fire (Jude 22-23). A study of both, and of the God who plucked Joshua from the fire and clothed him clean.

item.title: Run the Race: Come to Me, All Who Are Weary
item.description: Jesus invites the weary to Himself and gives them rest under His yoke. Hebrews tells tired believers to run with endurance, looking to Him. Why Christians grow weary, what feeds the runner, and what weighs the runner down.

item.title: When Love Grows Cold: The Falling Away and the Remnant
item.description: Jesus said the love of the many would grow cold. For the believer watching a friend's faith fade, Scripture adds Elijah's seven thousand, Isaiah's remnant, the disciples who fell away and were called back, and the Lord who knows those who are His.

item.title: "You Are Gods": Psalm 82, John 10 and the Authority God Lends
item.description: Psalm 82 calls those God set in authority אֱלֹהִים, "gods", and then sentences them by their works. Jesus quoted the psalm to the authorities who were judging Him, and rested His claim to be one with the Father on the Father's works, while their own works condemned them.

item.title: How God Answers Prayer
item.description: Heard at once, answered by varied routes and on God's own timetable, sometimes missed while it happens, and kept: what Scripture shows about the answers to prayer.

item.title: Those Called Gods: Judges, Angels and the Powers Over the Nations
item.description: Scripture lends the word אֱלֹהִים, "gods", to judges, to Moses, to heavenly beings and to the powers behind the nations, and Paul names the principalities and powers. Every one of them is "by nature not gods": God keeps His names and His glory to Himself, creates every power through His Son, and has disarmed them at the cross.

item.title: Take Up Your Cross
item.description: Peter rebuked Jesus for speaking of the cross, and Jesus called it setting the mind on the things of man. A study of Matthew 16:21-28 through two Greek word studies: the mind that keeps itself safe and high, the life saved by losing it, and Peter's own road from that rebuke to his denial, his tears and his restoration.

item.title: Test the Spirits: Recognising False Teachers and Wolves
item.description: The apostles expected false teachers to rise inside the church. Scripture tells you to keep testing every teacher by three marks: the Christ they preach, the life they live, and where they lead you. Signs, crowds and Bible words prove nothing, and the One in you is greater.

item.title: Recommended Bible Resources
item.description: Sites, tools and channels I use alongside these studies: short expositional answers, free study tooling, free Bibles, and biblical archaeology on location.

item.title: The Almond
item.description: Numbers 17 to Hebrews 7: the almond, whose Hebrew name sounds like 'watching', in the lampstand's gold blossoms and in Aaron's dead staff that budded, flowered and bore ripe almonds overnight to show whom God had chosen to come near Him, and the High Priest He appointed by the power of an indestructible life.

item.title: Four Hundred and Eighty Years: From the Exodus to Solomon's Temple
item.description: Why 1 Kings 6:1's 480 years from the Exodus to the temple holds once the judges are read as regional and Ruth's genealogy as telescoped, checked against the priestly and Davidic lines

item.title: Why Not 4004 BC? Where Ussher's Forty-Six Years Came From
item.description: Archbishop Ussher's creation date was printed in Bible margins for 250 years. His count from Adam to the Exodus still stands; forty-six years crept in while he added up the kings, and Kings itself shows how Israel's scribes actually counted.

item.title: The Cities of the Plain
item.description: Four cities overthrown by fire and one spared: what Genesis says about Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim and Zoar, how the rest of Scripture keeps the difference, Zoar on the sixth-century Madaba mosaic, the burned southern sites, and the sulphur balls.

item.title: Memory Verse Cards
item.description: Printable A4 sheets of Scripture memory cards: the Hebrew or Greek with transliteration and gloss, the ESV and the WEB.

item.title: Forgive Us Our Debts
item.description: God forgives by cancelling a debt you could never pay, and the forgiveness is received by everyone who repents. A study of Matthew 6:14-15: what biblical forgiveness is, how it differs from love and from trust, what to do when the one who wronged you keeps on, and how to forgive without false guilt.

item.title: Hurt by the Church: Wolves, Weeds and the Good Shepherd
item.description: People in church get hurt by the people they trusted. Scripture names four kinds of hurt: brothers who fail you, shepherds who harm, wolves who prey, and the weeds of the world. It answers each one differently, and it points every one of them to the Good Shepherd who stays.

item.title: Teaching the Lord's Prayer at Home
item.description: A seven-week household guide to the Lord's Prayer, one line a week: what each line shows about God, a Bible story, questions for children and adults, a practice for the home, a verse to learn, and Paul's prayers to pray over your children.
